From Eichhorn (“squirrel”) + -chen (“diminutive suffix”), folk etymology based on Eiche and Horn, but actually from Middle High German eichurne, from Old High German eihhorno, from Proto-West Germanic *aikwernō.

Eichel.et: From Middle High German eichel, from Old High German eihhila, from Proto-West Germanic *aikilā. Equivalent to Eiche (“oak”) + -el, alternative to Proto-West Germanic *-ilā (“fruit of the tree”). The sense “glans penis” is a semantic loan from Latin glāns.

eichen.et: From Middle High German eichen, īchen, from Old High German *īkōn, from Proto-West Germanic *īkwōn (“to measure, gauge”).
From Middle High German eichīn, from Old High German eihhīn, from Proto-Germanic *aikīnaz, equivalent to Eiche + -en.

Eichkatze.et: Equivalent to Eiche (“oak”) + Katze (“cat”). Cognate with Bavarian Oachkatzl and Aachkatzl.
